title: Access Review Orchestration Cheatsheet — Q2 2025
content:
Purpose:
This is a tactical cheatsheet for running the quarterly access review and least-privilege recertification in Q2 2025. Focus is on orchestration (who runs what when), what evidence to collect for audits, and automation hooks for SIEM export and evidence packaging. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — a blend of commands, queries, timelines, and troubleshooting notes for the on-call reviewer.

Context / scope:
- Applies to RBAC v2 roles across cloud consoles, Redwood internal admin panels, and the Dedicated control plane.
- Goal: identify stale/granted-but-unused privileges, enforce removal or documented exceptions, and produce a signed evidence bundle for auditors.
- Not a policy doc; use this alongside the policy matrix in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-SEC-1234).

Quick timeline (high level):
- Day -21: pre-run sanity checks (role counts, automation health, SIEM ingestion snapshot)
- Day -14: automated email to role owners with tentative list + remediation links
- Day -7: reminders + escalation list created in Jira
- Day 0: active review window opens (14 days)
- Day +14: final sweep, evidence package creation, upload to secure share, notify auditors

Pre-checks (Day -21):
- Verify RBAC v2 sync job status: kubectl -n rbac get jobs rbac-sync — check lastSuccessfulTime
- SIEM ingestion health (Splunk): search index=redwood_audit earliest=-48h | stats count by sourcetype — expect non-zero ingestions for audit events
- Confirm API token validity for automation user (service account: sec-audit-runner@redwood.com)
- Ensure key material accessible: KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/abcd-...

Extracting candidate list (example BigQuery / Postgres snippets):
- BigQuery (hosted audit logs):
  SELECT actor_email, rbac_role, resource_type, resource_id, action, COUNT(*) as uses, MAX(timestamp) as last_seen
  FROM `redwood-logs.audit.rbac_events`
  WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 180 DAY)
  GROUP BY actor_email, rbac_role, resource_type, resource_id, action
  HAVING uses = 0 OR MAX(timestamp) < TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
  ORDER BY last_seen ASC

- Postgres (internal admin DB):
  SELECT user_email, role_name, assigned_at, last_activity_at
  FROM rbac_assignments
  WHERE last_activity_at IS NULL OR last_activity_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'

SIEM export fields (required minimal schema for evidence):
- audit_event_id (string)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_email
- actor_id (internal user id)
- auth_mechanism (sso, api_key, service_account)
- action (e.g., role.assign, role.remove, token.create, console.login)
- resource_type (project, cluster, model, dataset, secret)
- resource_id
- rbac_role
- policy_version
- approval_ticket (if action had an approval flow)
- session_id
- request_id
- outcome (success|failure|denied)

Notes on PII & retention:
- Redact ip_address and user-agent from the evidence package unless explicitly requested by auditors. Store removed fields in internal SIEM only with access controls.
- Evidence bundle kept for 7 years per retention policy but shared artifact in audit folder is TTL'd to 90 days unless escalated.

Automation: packaging evidence (script checklist)
- Runner: sec-audit-runner (GitHub actions / scheduled job)
- Steps executed by runner:
  1) Pull RBAC assignments snapshot: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/rbac/v2/assignments?as_of=2025-04-01 -o assignments.csv
  2) Pull SIEM query results for the same window: bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "<query above>" --format=csv > usage.csv
  3) Run diff heuristics: python tools/recert/detect_orphans.py assignments.csv usage.csv --out orphans.csv
  4) Create Jira ticket(s) for auto-flagged orphans: python tools/recert/create_jira.py orphans.csv --project SEC
  5) Bundle: tar -czvf evidence_bundle_q2_2025.tar.gz assignments.csv usage.csv orphans.csv runbook.txt
  6) Encrypt bundle with KMS and upload to s3://redwood-audit-archives/q2-2025/evidence_bundle_q2_2025.tar.gz.enc

Evidence checklist (for auditors):
- RBAC snapshot (assignments.csv) with role hashes masked for PII
- SIEM usage report (usage.csv) showing last seen timestamp for each assignment
- Orphan detection output (orphans.csv) with recommended action and confidence score
- Jira tickets for exceptions (links and ticket IDs)
- Signed attestation: PDF signed by security lead and product owner (template at CONFLUENCE-SEC-1234)
- Runbook version and runner logs (GitHub Actions run id)

Exception handling / approvals:
- If owner requests exception > 90 days, require documented business reason + compensating control + exact expiry date. Create Jira ticket with tag sec:recert-exception and link to approval_ticket field.
- Exceptions > 180 days must go to VP Security for approval. Track in spreadsheet: exceptions-q2-2025.csv

Common gotchas + troubleshooting notes:
- Duplicate identities: SSO->SCIM mapping sometimes duplicates emails; run tools/ids/normalize_identities.py first and note mapping.csv in bundle
- Service accounts showing as orphaned: filter by auth_mechanism = service_account and verify last token creation event before auto-removal
- RBAC v2 policy version skew: if assignments reference policy_version < 3.1 runrbac-migration-checker and annotate tickets
- SIEM ingestion lag: split window into two runs if max(timestamp) < now()-1h; rerun ingestion pipeline (datapipeline/ingest-audit pipeline) prior to packaging

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
- Day -14 owner non-response: ping owner + CC product manager
- Day -7 escalate to team lead: @Owen Li
- Day -2 escalate to Dir Security: @Priya Nair
- If evidence packaging fails: page infra-oncall and sec-oncall (pagerduty IDs in Confluence header)

Sample Splunk query for suspicious role grants (detect manual bypasses):
  index=redwood_audit sourcetype=rbac_events action=role.assign earliest=-180d@d
  | stats latest(timestamp) as last, count by actor_email, target_email, rbac_role, policy_version
  | where count < 3 AND last < relative_time(now(), "-90d")

Packaging & sign-off (Day +14):
- Security lead (Maya) and PM owner must append signed attestation.pdf into archive
- Upload encrypted bundle and paste location in Jira epic SEC-RECERT-Q2-2025
- Post final message to #sec-recert channel with summary csv and link to archive (do not include sensitive fields in Slack)

Followup (post recert):
- Run a 30-day follow-up query to ensure removals executed and no re-grants occurred unintentionally. Document in audit-trace.log
- Update RBAC gap list and feed into the RBAC v2 backlog (github: /issues labeled rbac-v2)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to include near-real-time Slack approvals (yes/no)? Risk: approvals recorded only in Slack history (harder to ingest) — TODO: proposal to add an approval API by June 2025 (owner: Samir)
- What is acceptable confidence threshold for auto-closure of orphan tickets? current default is confidence >= 0.85 but needs review by product teams.

Notes to self:
- Keep bundle size under 200MB for easy upload to s3 and quick reviewer downloads. If larger, split by team and produce per-team archives.
- Remind infra to bump SIEM TTL for audit indexes during recert window to avoid retention pruning.

References and follow-up reading:
- CONFLUENCE-SEC-1234 (recert policy)
- github.com/redwood-inference/org/rbac-v2 (migration notes)
- JIRA-SEC-4221 (automation epic)

Sign-off:
- Drafted by: Maya Patel (security)
- Reviewed by: Owen Li, Priya Nair
